<!-- factory:begin -->
## Factory machine

This machine runs a Hermes software factory. Its private configuration
record is the wiki page "Acme factory record",
https://wiki.example/acme-factory.
Read it before you change the machine's configuration, and update it in the
same change.

Keep the factory replicable. Every change to a factory environment also
lands in the factory repository in the same change, as a runbook step,
template, script, or check, so a fresh install reproduces it. A machine
state the runbook cannot reproduce is a defect. Real values go only to the
private record, never to the repository.

### GitHub

- Act on GitHub only as the factory's GitHub App, `acme-factory[bot]`.
  Run every `gh` command as
  `GH_CONFIG_DIR=/home/acme/.hermes/profiles/worker/gh gh <command>`.
- Never run `gh auth login`, never set `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and
  never ask the operator to sign in to GitHub.
- Publish commits only with
  `GH_CONFIG_DIR=/home/acme/.hermes/profiles/worker/gh python3 /home/acme/.hermes/profiles/worker/scripts/push-signed`.
  Never use `git push`.
- One exception: a worker uploads images for pull requests with
  `python3 /home/acme/.hermes/profiles/worker/scripts/github-upload-image`. The gateway uploads them
  with the operator's upload token. Never read, print, or use
  `GITHUB_UPLOAD_TOKEN` yourself, never pass it to `gh`, and never upload
  anything else through the broker.
- `Resource not accessible by integration` means the App lacks a
  permission. Report it to the operator. Do not switch identities.
- The App cannot create linked branches, so `gh issue develop` fails with a
  `createLinkedBranch` permission error. Derive the branch name with the
  repository's issue-tracker rule instead, and create the branch from the
  fetched default branch.

### Tools

- `gh` and the other tools setup installed live in `/home/acme/.local/bin`. A
  non-login shell can lack that directory on `PATH`, so call a tool by its
  full path when the bare name is not found. Do not install a second copy.

### Secrets

- Hermes loads the factory's secrets from Infisical, environment
  `prod`, folder `/factory`, when it starts: the gateway through
  `~/.hermes/bin/factory-secrets`, and the worker through its own
  `scripts/worker-secrets`, which keeps only the worker's three keys.
  Never print, copy, or move a secret, and never ask for one in chat. When
  a new secret is needed, ask the operator to enter it in their own
  terminal.
- Never run `hermes config get` with `--raw`, and never run a secrets
  helper such as `factory-secrets`, `worker-secrets`, or `proxy-token` by
  hand. Each prints secret values. To check a secret, compare it in memory and print a
  boolean, or list variable names only.
- These credentials are for the operator only, and Hermes agents never
  receive them: `OP_TOKEN`, the 1Password service account
  that interactive shells reach through `op`.
- Never run `op`, and never read the operator-only credentials, even when a
  login shell puts an `op` wrapper on `PATH`.

### Linear

- To read a Linear agent session from its URL or ID, run
  `python3 ~/.hermes/plugins/linear-agent-session/cli.py session <url-or-id>`.
  It prints every activity, oldest first.
- The command gets the app's token from the gateway's broker and never prints
  it. Never read the token, and never call the plugin's client inline.
- Posting into an agent session is not available to operator sessions.

### Remote access and ingress

- The factory's tunnel routes and Cloudflare Access applications are code in
  `infra` of the `acme/product` repository. Merging
  its pull request into `main` deploys them. Never change Cloudflare in the
  dashboard or with the `cloudflared` CLI. The running tunnel's routes are in
  the `cloudflared` service log, under "Updated to new configuration".
- People SSH in as `acme` at `ssh.acme.example` through Cloudflare Access
  short-lived certificates, or with a key. sshd never accepts a password. Do
  not turn password login back on.
- One list says who may SSH in: the SSH allowlist in `infra` of the
  `acme/product` repository. The machine
  mirrors it in `/etc/ssh/authorized_principals/acme`, one email local
  part per line. Change both in the same change.
- After any change to SSH, sharing, or the firewall, run
  `python3 ~/acme/factory/skills/setup-factory/scripts/check-host-exposure --ssh-users a@acme.example,b@acme.example`.
  Every line must start with `PASS`.

### Privileged steps

- You cannot answer a `sudo` password prompt. Put the privileged commands
  in one script in your scratch directory, make it refuse a change that
  could lock someone out, and ask the operator to run it with `sudo` in
  their own terminal. Name the terminal and the exact command, then wait.

### Factory processes

- The worker profile `/home/acme/.hermes/profiles/worker` owns the checkouts at
  `~/acme/product` and `~/acme/factory`.
  Change them only through a Kanban card.
- The gateway runs as a service. Restart it only when the operator asks,
  from a shell outside Hermes. Two launchd jobs also restart it, each
  through `restart-gateway`. `watch-gateway` restarts a gateway whose
  secrets did not resolve. `auto-deploy` restarts it after it installs a
  merged factory change that needs a restart. Leave both running.
- `auto-deploy` deploys each merge to the factory's default branch. While
  it installs, it holds `factory-gateway.lock`. To fix what it reports, or
  to deploy by hand, follow the setup-factory runbook's "Deploy a merged
  factory change" section.
  `HERMES_HOME=/home/acme/.hermes/profiles/worker python3 /home/acme/.hermes/profiles/worker/scripts/check-install` lists what is out of
  date.
